t: You're looking at a bronze statue of Sir Nigel Gresley, standing near the booking office of King's Cross station. Gresley was a locomotive designer who worked in offices at this station, and he rose to be Chief Mechanical Engineer of the London and North Eastern Railway. His engines include the Flying Scotsman, the first steam locomotive officially recorded over a hundred miles an hour in passenger service, and Mallard, which still holds the world steam speed record of 126 miles an hour. The sculptor is Hazel Reeves, and the Gresley Society commissioned the statue in his memory.
